text:
alex: Deploybot alerted p95 regression for embeddings after the new attention kernel flag. Canary at 20% paused. Should we hotfix the flag or rollback to previous model build?

deploybot: AUTOMATION: rollout_paused reason=p95_latency(>2s) suggested_action=manual_review

maya: Looks like kvcache miss rate + memory churn immediately after the flag flip. I can flip the flag back on canary as a targeted hotfix while we triage.

sam: I prefer pin-and-shift to v3.4.1 for stability. Hotfix is faster but leaves deployment state undocumented. If we pin, we'll have a clear rollback history.

irene: Ops checklist: create ASANA ticket, update release notes line to say "reverted kernel flag" and notify CS and legal if customers report incidents. @natalie can draft the external blurb.

natalie: Draft external: "We've reverted a recent performance tweak after observing higher latency on some embeddings requests. We restored the previous configuration for canary while we investigate; no customer data exposure."

alex: Proposed sequence: 1) maya runs a hotfix env flip on canary and watches metrics, 2) if stable, sam pins model to v3.4.1 and shifts canary traffic to pinned rollout, 3) alex sends internal and external comms + create postmortem ticket. Agree? :thumbsup:

maya: Hotfix command: ```kubectl set env deploy/infer-runtime KERNEL_FLAG=off -n inference-canary``` I'll execute and monitor p95 + kvcache hit rate.
sam: Pin/shift commands I'll run after maya confirms stability: `redwoodctl rollout pin --model embeddings --version v3.4.1 --scope canary` then `redwoodctl traffic shift --from new:canary --to pinned:canary --percent 100`.
deploybot: ACTION_LOG user=maya action=env_update target=inference-canary status=queued

maya: Hotfix applied. Observing telemetry now.
deploybot: TELEMETRY p95_latency embeddings canary 2.8s -> 1.0s over 2m. rollout_resume=false

sam: Stability good for 3m. Applying pin and shifting traffic now.
sam: Commands completed: pin=status=ok traffic_shift=status=complete. Canary now pinned to v3.4.1 and at 100% canary traffic.
alex: Thanks team. I'm posting the external blurb and notifying #prod-alerts and CS. I'll open the ASANA postmortem and attach logs.
irene: ASANA-9876 created and assigned to eng-ml for root-cause. CS notified and blurb posted with FAQ for support.
natalie: External note posted to customers. Support FAQ added. Closing thread.
